history.period: Ancient origins (traditionally said to date to the Zamorin period; some secondary sources claim 14th century - verify); renamed from Arikkodikkavu to Azhakodi Devi Mahashekthram in 1965
history.summary: Azhakodi Devi Temple at Thiruthiyad, within Kozhikode city, is one of the famous Devi temples of Malabar and is administered by the Malabar Devaswom Board. Legend holds that the Samoothiri entrusted six of his generals to this temple (then called Arikkodikkavu) and gave them an idol of Bhavani Devi, a gift to him from Gujarati traders, to be installed beside the Bhagavathi idol in the sreekovil - making it reportedly the only temple in Kerala where two Devi forms are worshipped together as primary deities. The site was once an islet called Thuruthnadu (later Thiruthiyadu). A subsidiary grove shrine (Kizhakkekavu) to Bhuvaneshwari, believed to be the kalari devata of the Tiruthiyadaruvar, completes the complex after the noon pooja in the main temple.

town_description: Kozhikode (Calicut) is a major coastal city in northern Kerala and the historic seat of the Zamorin dynasty. A famed medieval trading port of the Malabar coast, it is known for its spices, beaches, and vibrant food and football culture. The temple sits at Thiruthiyad, close to the heart of the city.
